Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int \frac{{ln}^{5}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{5}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{5{ln}^{4}⁡x}{x}, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{4x}\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{5}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{5}⁡x)(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})(\frac{5{ln}^{4}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{4}-5\int \frac{{ln}^{5}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{4}-5I.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $I.$ We can ignore the constant of integration in this case, because it is insignificant for further evaluation of the definite integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{4}-5I \\ 6I & =\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{4} \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{24}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{{ln}^{5}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{24}({ln}^{6}⁡x)\,{|}_{1}^{{e}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}({ln}^{6}⁡({e}^{3})-{ln}^{6}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}((3\operatorname{ln}⁡e)^{6}-{0}^{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}({3}^{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{243}{8}\end{aligned}
$$
